title: On-demand stream rewrite with compact tombstone index for retroactive PII scrubbing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a service and operator patterns that enable targeted, on-demand rewriting of historical analytics event streams to remove or pseudonymize PII without re-ingesting every downstream materialized view. The approach pairs a compact tombstone index referencing affected shards/time-windows with a replayable 'cassette' of transformation records. Goals: minimize reprocessing cost, preserve audit trail, ensure deterministic redaction, and support selective rollback for false positives.
motivation: We frequently need to apply retroactive deletions or redactions due to consent changes, legal requests, or discovered leak patterns. Full backfill reprocessing is slow, expensive, and risks divergence across materialized views. A targeted replay approach reduces cost and outage surface while providing verifiable auditability for compliance teams.
scope: Prototype tombstone indexing + rewrite operator for Kafka topics and internal event lake. Integrations for Console metrics views and short-term analytics dashboards. Exclude long-term aggregated OLAP re-computations from MVP (they will consume tombstone exports).
acceptance_criteria: Service can generate a compact tombstone index for a specified customer_id and time range within 15 minutes for 30 days of events
Rewrite operator can replay events through redaction pipeline and emit rewrite events to a separate topic (rewrite-topic) without changing original raw topic
Materialized views for console counts and latency dashboards can subscribe to rewrite-topic and apply idempotent updates within 5% of baseline latency
Audit log records produced for each rewrite operation contain: initiating user, request id, tombstone keys, transformation hash, and checksum of pre/post counts
End-to-end privacy verification harness demonstrates that a sample of 10k events containing PII tokens are removed or pseudonymized deterministically
Can abort and rollback a rewrite if a validation job detects >0.1% unintended field changes
Conspicuous metrics and SLOs added to observability dashboard: rewrite-latency, rewrite-success-rate, tombstone-index-generation-time
design_decisions: Use tombstone index separate from original log to avoid modifying raw immutable event streams
Emit rewrite events rather than mutating original topics to preserve provenance and enable auditing
Represent tombstones as compact (shard, start_ts, end_ts, key-fingerprint) rows for fast lookups
Leverage existing replay framework from ENG-56478 where possible; add a lightweight cassette format for transformation steps
Make rewrites idempotent using event-level sequence and checksum fields
Perform transformations in a sidecar process to limit blast radius and simplify rollout
implementation_notes: Tombstone index stored in a small RocksDB-backed service with TTL and snapshot export
Replay mechanism reads original topic at offsets marked by tombstone index and produces to rewrite-topic with an extra header 'redacted: true'
Downstream materialized view adapters will be updated to reconcile rewrite-topic messages by applying upserts based on (primary_key, window_start)
Transformation cassette format: newline-delimited JSON with op, selectors, replacement strategy, applied_by, applied_at, and sha256
Provide a migration tool to generate tombstone indexes from existing per-customer deletion manifests
Ensure all network calls to tombstone index store are authenticated using mTLS and service account tokens
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed to measure cost of full reprocess vs targeted replay for 30-day shard (benchmarked on staging cluster). Targeted replay is ~8x cheaper for medium-size customers.
2026-02-18: Schema for compact tombstone index drafted; reviewed with infra and privacy. Decided to include key-fingerprint instead of plaintext keys to reduce leakage risk.
2026-02-25: Initial prototype of cassette writer implemented (libcassette v0.1). Emits transformation steps and checksum metadata. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/replay-proto/pull/72
2026-03-02: Integration test harness running in ephemeral env. Verified idempotency by replaying same cassette twice; materialized view adapters deduplicated correctly.
2026-03-08: Security review kickoff with SSO and key-management team. Raised question on whether cassette files should be encrypted at rest; decided to encrypt with KMS-managed keys for MVP.
2026-03-10: Started building operator to apply rewrites to staging console dashboards. Observability hooks added to prometheus (rewrite_jobs_total, rewrite_failures_total).
reviews_and_feedback: PM review (Rafael Mendes): Emphasized need for admin UI to initiate and monitor rewrites; requested ability to preview impact before commit.
Privacy review (Dr. Elena Park): Approved use of key-fingerprint; requested tighter retention on tombstone indexes (default 90 days) and audit export format for legal holds.
Infra review (Priya Nair): Recommended limiting parallel rewrite workers per shard to avoid Kafka consumer group overload; suggested backpressure windowing.
Design review (Marta Liu): Asked that transformation cassette be human-readable and include provenance details for SOC audits
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Rewrite may produce transient inconsistencies in derived metrics. Mitigation: Add delayed reconciliation job that cross-checks pre/post totals and emits alerts if delta > threshold.
Risk: Tombstone index could leak sensitive keys. Mitigation: Store only fingerprints and rotate index encryption keys; restrict access via RBAC.
Risk: Large customers generate huge tombstone sets. Mitigation: Provide batching API and shard-prioritization; allow customer-scoped sampling for low-impact rewrites.
Risk: Misapplied transformations causing data corruption. Mitigation: Dry-run mode with impact preview and automatic rollback on validation failures.
Risk: Operator complexity adds maintenance burden. Mitigation: Keep core rewrite engine minimal and implement adapters as small, well-tested sidecar services
qa_plan: Unit tests for cassette encoding/decoding and checksum verification
Integration tests: small, medium, large replay against staging topics with synthetic PII payloads
End-to-end privacy verification: run evaluation harness to ensure PII tokens absent after rewrite
Canary rollout: apply rewrites to a single non-production customer namespace and monitor metrics for 48 hours
Load test: simulate concurrent rewrites across 50 shards to validate backpressure and worker limits
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): Tombstone index + replay service + rewrite-topic; adapters for console short-term views; staging-only rollout
Phase 2: Admin UI for replay requests, dry-run preview, and audit exports; encryption-at-rest for cassettes; production pilot with 5 customers
Phase 3: Support aggregated OLAP re-compute hooks and legal-hold freeze; SLA and runbook for large backfills
